items.title: llm 0.37
items.snippet: Release: llm 0.37 There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes. I added gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra , plus a new llm openai endpoint add command to make it easier to configure additional models that use OpenAI-compatible endpoints. I switched the default model (if you have not set your own default) to gpt-6-luna - half the price of the previous default, gpt-5.6-luna . LLM's support for embeddi

items.summary_ar: أصدر Simon Willison الإصدار 0.37 من أداة LLM CLI ومكتبة Python، ويجمع ميزات وإصلاحات تراكمت خلال نحو شهرين. أضاف الإصدار موديلين هما gpt-6.1-sol و gpt-6.1-terra، إلى جانب أمر llm openai endpoint add لتسهيل إعداد موديلات تعمل عبر OpenAI-compatible endpoints. وتغيّر الموديل الافتراضي إلى gpt-6-luna بنصف سعر الموديل السابق gpt-5.6-luna.

items.title_en: llm 0.37 adds GPT-6.1 models and an OpenAI endpoint command
items.summary_en: Simon Willison released llm 0.37, the CLI tool and Python library, bundling about two months of features and fixes. It adds gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra, plus a new llm openai endpoint add command for OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The default model switches to gpt-6-luna, which is half the price of the previous default gpt-5.6-luna.
items.why_en: It is a tool you can install and test immediately to compare models and wire up OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

items.title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
items.snippet: Recently, harness self-evolution has emerged as an important paradigm for improving agent performance. Prior studies show that evolving the agent harness can effectively enhance agent capabilities without modifying the foundation model's parameters. We find that existing approaches largely study agent evolution on a single task. In practice, coding agents may need to handle multiple task types over time. Whether an agent harness can continuously evolve across multiple tasks without suffering from catastrophic forgetting remains an important open question. In this paper, we investigate this open question through a comprehensive empirical study of continual harness self-evolution. We organize
items.title_ar: هل تستطيع coding agents التطور المستمر دون نسيان؟
items.summary_ar: تدرس الورقة قدرة agent harness على التطور المستمر عبر أنواع متعددة من المهام البرمجية، دون ما يعرف بـ catastrophic forgetting. تقدم دراسة تجريبية شاملة لهذا السؤال المفتوح، مع الإبقاء على parameters الموديل الأساسي دون تعديل.
items.why_ar: يهمك لأنه يرتبط مباشرة بتصميم coding agents داخلياً والحفاظ على أدائها عبر مهام متعددة.
items.title_en: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
items.summary_en: The paper studies whether an agent harness can keep evolving across multiple coding task types without catastrophic forgetting. It presents a comprehensive empirical study of continual harness self-evolution. The foundation model parameters are not modified.
items.why_en: It is directly relevant to building coding agents that keep their performance across multiple task types.

items.title: SIMIT: Self-Improving Vision-Language Models via Imagination at Test-Time
items.snippet: We introduce SIMIT, a test-time self-improvement framework in which a vision-language model creates its own query-specific training data before answering an unlabeled test query. Our goal is to improve performance on a given target test set without annotations or external models. To pursue this goal, some test-time methods improve answers through longer reasoning or repeated sampling but leave the model unchanged. Others update the model using rewards based on majority agreement among multiple candidate answers or the model's own judgments of correctness, but such rewards can reinforce existing mistakes. SIMIT instead imagines similar problems whose solutions it controls: a model need not co
items.title_ar: SIMIT: تحسين vision-language models أثناء الاختبار عبر التخيل الذاتي
items.summary_ar: يقدم الإطار SIMIT طريقة self-improvement أثناء الاختبار، حيث يولّد الموديل بيانات تدريب خاصة بكل استعلام قبل الإجابة على سؤال غير موسوم. يتجنب الإطار المكافآت القائمة على إجماع الإجابات أو تقييم الموديل لنفسه، لأنها قد تعزز الأخطاء الموجودة. الهدف تحسين الأداء على مجموعة الاختبار المستهدفة دون annotations أو نماذج خارجية.
items.why_ar: يفيد في تحسين أنظمة الرؤية واللغة على بيانات بنكية غير موسومة دون إعادة تدريب كاملة.
items.title_en: SIMIT: Self-improving vision-language models via test-time imagination
items.summary_en: SIMIT lets a vision-language model generate query-specific training data before answering an unlabeled test query. It avoids majority-agreement rewards and self-judged correctness, which can reinforce existing mistakes. The goal is to improve performance on a target test set without annotations or external models.
items.why_en: It offers a way to adapt vision-language systems to unlabeled banking data without full retraining.

items.title: Can Large Language Model Agents Learn by Watching Tutorial Videos?
items.snippet: Humans continuously acquire knowledge from carefully crafted materials such as books and tutorial videos, carrying that understanding into future tasks. Millions of such instructional videos are uploaded online every day, yet LLM agents remain unable to exploit this ever-expanding wealth of human teaching. Their capabilities are frozen after training, while parameter updates at scale remain prohibitively expensive. This raises the central question: can LLM agents learn from this vast instructional resource without parameter updates? We introduce Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL), a nonparametric continual-learning paradigm that consolidates tutorial videos into a persistent, structured tutoria
items.title_ar: هل يتعلم LLM agents من فيديوهات الشروحات دون تحديث الأوزان؟
items.summary_ar: تقدم الورقة Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL)، وهو نمط تعلم مستمر غير parametric يحول فيديوهات الشروحات إلى قاعدة معرفة مهيكلة ودائمة. الفكرة أن الوكيل يستفيد من هذه المعرفة دون تكلفة تحديث parameters على نطاق واسع.
items.why_ar: يهم المهندس لأنه يقدم نمطاً لتحسين agents دون fine-tuning وبتكلفة أقل.
items.title_en: Can LLM Agents Learn by Watching Tutorial Videos?
items.summary_en: The paper introduces Tutorial Agentic Learning (TAL), a nonparametric continual-learning paradigm that consolidates tutorial videos into a persistent, structured knowledge base. The goal is to let agents use this instructional material without expensive parameter updates.
items.why_en: It presents a low-cost, non-fine-tuning pattern for improving agents, which is useful for his agent work.

items.title: Lab2Sim: Turning Real-World Experiment Videos into Interactive Virtual Experiments
items.snippet: Science experiment videos demonstrate how experiments are performed, but offer no direct interaction for learners. Turning them into virtual experiments requires not only reproducing the observed apparatus and state changes, but also enforcing the preconditions governing each operation. We introduce Lab2Sim, a benchmark of 218 science experiment videos with evidence-grounded specifications and 11,881 rubric items. To address this task, we propose EduVideo2Code, which extracts experimental procedures hierarchically, encodes them as explicit state machines to guide code generation, and refines the resulting pages through execution-based verification. items.title_en: Lab2Sim: turning experiment videos into interactive simulations
items.summary_en: The paper introduces Lab2Sim, a benchmark of 218 science experiment videos with 11,881 rubric items. It also proposes EduVideo2Code, which extracts procedures hierarchically, encodes them as state machines to guide code generation, and refines outputs through execution-based verification.
items.why_en: It is a useful reference for evaluating multimodal models on video-to-code generation, a research area close to your work.

items.title: When Morphs Look Better: Face Image Quality as a Training-Free Signal for Morphing Attack Detection
items.snippet: Face image quality assessment (FIQA) estimates the utility of a face image for automated face recognition and has been proposed as a morphing attack detection (MAD) signal that requires no morph-specific training. We evaluate 17 FIQA methods from all current FIQA categories on 20 morphing attack sets from two datasets, FRLL and FEI, including five diffusion-based attack sets. Each quality score is used directly as a MAD decision score. Unlike prior work, which inverted a quality measure when this lowered its error, we fix the score direction of each method in advance from its definition, so that cases in which morphs receive higher quality than bona fide samples remain visible. items.title_ar: جودة صورة الوجه كإشارة بلا تدريب لكشف morphing attack
items.summary_ar: يقيّم البحث 17 طريقة لتقدير جودة صورة الوجه (FIQA) ويستخدم درجة الجودة مباشرةً كقرار لكشف morphing attack دون أي تدريب خاص بالهجمات. تشمل التجربة 20 مجموعة هجمات من FRLL وFEI، بينها خمس مجموعات مبنية على diffusion. الجديد أن اتجاه الدرجة يُحدد مسبقاً لكل طريقة بدل عكسه لتحسين النتائج، فتظهر الحالات التي تحصل فيها الصور المزيفة على جودة أعلى من الصور الحقيقية.
items.why_ar: كشف الوجوه المزيفة في التحقق الرقمي من الهوية وفتح الحسابات مشكلة مباشرة في البنوك.
items.title_en: Face image quality as a training-free signal for morphing attack detection
items.summary_en: The paper evaluates 17 face image quality assessment (FIQA) methods as direct morphing attack detection scores, with no morph-specific training. The evaluation covers 20 attack sets from FRLL and FEI, including five diffusion-based sets. Each method's score direction is fixed in advance from its definition, so cases where morphs score higher than bona fide samples stay visible.
